description: A Spanish-first internal CRM that lets a non-technical sales team maintain normalized prospect data, manage follow-up work, and answer governed business questions without using SQL.

source_artifacts.purpose: Approved product, architecture, migration, security, and delivery baseline
Normalized pre-SQL migration source and reconciliation baseline
Initial relational-model proposal; Django migrations become authoritative once implemented

agent_workflow.orchestrator: Owns feature selection, specification readiness, dependencies, state transitions, and final closure; it does not edit application implementation while coordinating a feature.
agent_workflow.implementer: Implements exactly one selected feature and its verification without reviewing or approving its own work.
agent_workflow.validator: Independently inspects the specification, actual diff, tests, and runtime evidence; it never edits implementation files.
agent_workflow.explorer: Optionally answers one bounded read-only question before implementation and records evidence on disk.

architecture_constraints: Use Python 3.12 or later with Django 5.2 LTS.
Use a modular monolith with explicit CRM, activity, data-quality, reporting, identity, and platform boundaries.
Use server-rendered Django templates enhanced progressively with HTMX and locally vendored Bootstrap assets.
Use PostgreSQL 18 as the production system of record; SQLite must not be used to validate PostgreSQL-specific behavior.
Keep business rules in application services and database constraints rather than templates, views, or ad hoc scripts.
Use PostgreSQL full-text search and pg_trgm before introducing a separate search service.
Use a PostgreSQL transactional outbox worker before introducing Redis, Celery, or a message broker.
Use governed reporting views and metric definitions; do not expose arbitrary SQL to users.
Use OIDC with provider-managed MFA as the target authentication method, with local accounts only as a documented temporary fallback.
Preserve raw source evidence, normalized values, lineage, aliases, status history, and append-only audit events.
Archive routine business records instead of destructive deletion; immutable source, history, and audit records are not user-deletable.
Store timestamps in UTC and display business dates in America/Argentina/Cordoba unless a team-specific timezone is configured.
Do not store patient identifiers, pathology results, or clinical case data; this is a sales CRM, not a clinical system.
Do not add microservices, a SPA framework, a data warehouse, or free-form AI-to-SQL in the MVP without an approved architecture decision.
definition_of_ready: The feature has a bounded user or platform outcome and explicit in-scope and out-of-scope statements.
All dependency features are done or the orchestrator documents why the dependency is not required.
Every requirement and acceptance criterion has a stable unique identifier.
Acceptance criteria are observable and have an automated test or a justified manual procedure.
Permissions, data ownership, failure behavior, migration impact, and rollback implications are specified when applicable.
There are no unresolved questions that would materially change the implementation.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion has concrete evidence in the implementation and validation reports.
The configured fast verification command and all feature-specific verification commands pass.
The implementation follows the architecture, conventions, security, privacy, and accessibility contracts.
Database changes include reviewed migrations, constraints, rollback considerations, and representative tests.
User-facing changes include Spanish copy, understandable errors, permissions, responsive behavior, and empty states.
No unrelated changes, debug artifacts, secrets, or generated caches are included.
An independent validator records APPROVED and the orchestrator records both report paths before setting the feature to done.
success_metrics: At least 90 percent of active sellers use the application on four or more workdays per week during the first 90 days.
At least 90 percent of completed contacts are logged within 24 hours.
At least 95 percent of open in-progress leads have a next task or a documented reason.
No error-level migration item remains unresolved at cutover and fewer than 5 percent of active records have warnings after 60 days.
Every management KPI has an owner, definition, timeframe, scope, and fixture-backed expected result.
The median quick-contact workflow takes less than 60 seconds in usability testing.
The service achieves 99.5 percent monthly availability after launch.
List and search interactions meet a 500 millisecond p95 server-response target at the agreed initial data volume; standard dashboards meet a 2 second p95 target.
deferred_scope: Marketing automation and mass-email campaign orchestration
Billing, inventory, contracts, and ERP functions
Patient, specimen, pathology-result, or other clinical workflows
A generic opportunity, quote, or revenue-forecast model unless discovery proves it is required
A separate search cluster or analytics warehouse before measured PostgreSQL limits
Free-form natural-language-to-SQL or any autonomous write-capable AI agent

features.title: Spec-driven agent delivery harness
features.user_story: As the workflow owner, I need orchestrator, implementer, and validator agents to execute one approved feature at a time with durable evidence.

requirements.statement: Make orchestrator, implementer, and validator the canonical role names; retain explorer as an optional read-only supporting role.
Define exclusive ownership of feature state, implementation files, implementation reports, and validation reports.
Require the orchestrator task envelope to include feature ID, requirements, acceptance IDs, dependencies, allowed scope, report path, baseline revision, and exact verification commands.
Extend harness validation to check dependency integrity, one active feature, required report paths, legal status transitions, and evidence for every acceptance criterion.
Provide reusable implementation and validation report templates and update all runtime adapters to reference the canonical roles.
Add automated tests for harness metadata checks and configure a non-empty deterministic verification command.

acceptance.criterion: The canonical workflow is orchestrator to optional explorer to implementer to validator to orchestrator closure, with a documented changes-requested loop.
acceptance.evidence: Role files, AGENTS.md, and adapter inspection

acceptance.criterion: The harness rejects duplicate IDs, missing dependencies, dependency cycles, more than one active feature, missing acceptance evidence, and a done feature without an approved validation report.
acceptance.evidence: Automated positive and negative harness tests

acceptance.criterion: The implementer cannot be designated as validator for the same feature, and the validator is instructed to change only its report file.
acceptance.evidence: Metadata validation and role-contract test fixtures

acceptance.criterion: Running crm/init.sh executes both harness validation and the configured project verification command successfully.

features.title: Django project and developer foundation
features.user_story: As a developer, I need a reproducible Django application skeleton so every later feature shares the same tested foundation.

requirements.statement: Create the Django project under the existing src layout with explicit modules for config, CRM, activity, data quality, reporting, identity, and platform concerns.
Provide development, test, staging, and production settings with environment-variable configuration and safe production defaults.
Configure Spanish as the primary UI language, UTC storage, and America/Argentina/Cordoba display timezone.
Add deterministic commands for formatting, linting, type checking, tests, migrations checks, and Django deployment checks.
Expose liveness and readiness endpoints that do not disclose secrets or internal diagnostics.

acceptance.criterion: A clean UV environment can install the lockfile, run Django system checks, and execute the complete fast verification script.
The application starts with documented development settings and renders a Spanish landing or sign-in page without a JavaScript build step.
acceptance.evidence: Django integration test and manual browser check

acceptance.criterion: Readiness fails when its required database dependency is unavailable while liveness remains suitable for process monitoring.
acceptance.evidence: Endpoint tests with available and unavailable database

acceptance.criterion: Production configuration rejects missing secret keys, debug mode, insecure cookies, and invalid host configuration.
acceptance.evidence: Settings tests and Django deployment check

features.title: PostgreSQL persistence and environment configuration
features.user_story: As the technical owner, I need PostgreSQL-backed persistence and repeatable environments so production behavior is tested before release.

requirements.statement: Use PostgreSQL 18 for development integration, staging, production, and database-specific automated tests.
Configure connections from DATABASE_URL with bounded connection lifetimes, transaction-safe settings, and no credentials committed to source control.
Enable required PostgreSQL extensions through migrations, including pg_trgm when search is introduced.
Vendor and version Bootstrap and HTMX assets locally and collect versioned static assets for production.
Document environment bootstrap, migration, fixture, reset, and verification procedures without destructive broad-path commands.

acceptance.criterion: Migrations apply from an empty PostgreSQL database and re-running migrations is a no-op.
Application startup fails with an actionable error when required database configuration is absent or malformed.
The main page loads all required CSS and HTMX assets without a public CDN or Node.js runtime.
acceptance.evidence: Static-file integration test and network inspection

acceptance.criterion: No secret, real credential, or production customer data is present in tracked configuration or test fixtures.
acceptance.evidence: Repository secret scan and fixture review

features.title: Reference catalogs and controlled taxonomies
features.user_story: As a data steward, I need controlled catalogs so stages, channels, outcomes, specialties, campaigns, and geography remain consistent while labels stay understandable.

requirements.statement: Model campaign, lead status, interaction channel, interaction outcome, specialty, country, province, and locality as controlled reference data.
Use immutable stable codes and editable Spanish display labels, sort order, active state, and effective behavior flags.
Prevent deactivation or code changes from corrupting historical records; inactive values remain readable but unavailable for new selection.
Seed approved baseline values through idempotent data migrations or versioned fixtures.
Restrict catalog maintenance to data stewards or system administrators and audit every change.

acceptance.criterion: Repeated baseline loading produces exactly one row per stable code and does not overwrite an explicitly approved label change.
Inactive reference values remain visible on existing records but cannot be selected for new records.
Unauthorized users cannot create, edit, reorder, or deactivate catalog entries through direct URLs or crafted requests.
Foreign keys and uniqueness constraints prevent unknown and duplicate reference codes independently of form validation.

features.title: Identity, roles, teams, and scoped authorization
features.user_story: As a seller, I need to sign in safely and see only the sales records and actions assigned to my role and team.

requirements.statement: Support sales representative, sales manager, data steward, report viewer, privacy/audit reviewer, and system administrator roles.
Apply deny-by-default authorization using both an action permission and an object/team/campaign scope.
Use OIDC authorization-code flow with provider MFA and centralized disablement; provide a documented Argon2 local-account fallback only when OIDC is unavailable.
Treat view, create, change, reassign, merge, import, resolve-quality, audit-view, and bulk-export as distinct permissions.
Support temporary administrative elevation with reason, approver, expiry, and audit event.
Centralize scope-aware query services so search, detail pages, reports, exports, and direct object URLs apply identical visibility rules.

acceptance.criterion: A disabled identity cannot establish a session and an existing session is invalidated according to the documented offboarding policy.
Every role/action/scope combination has an automated allow-or-deny test, including cross-owner direct IDs and search results.
View permission alone never grants bulk export, merge, import, reassignment, or catalog-management capability.
Temporary elevation expires automatically and every use records actor, reason, scope, approval, and timestamp.
No UI navigation item or server endpoint exposes an unauthorized function or out-of-scope record.

out_of_scope: Building a new enterprise identity provider

features.title: Parties, organizations, people, and contact points
features.user_story: As a seller, I need a single understandable record for each organization or person and reliable ways to contact them.

requirements.statement: Model a party as exactly one person or organization subtype and support explicit person-to-organization relationships with role and effective dates.
Store one atomic contact value per contact point with type, raw value, normalized value, verification state, active state, suppression state, and provenance.
Normalize email case and phone numbers to E.164 when possible while retaining the original evidence.
Support specialties, addresses, province/locality, aliases, websites, and generic organizational contact points without misclassifying them as personal identifiers.
Use lifecycle state and optimistic concurrency so archive and concurrent edits are explicit and recoverable.
Warn on exact email or phone matches and plausible name/organization matches before creating a party, but never perform an automatic fuzzy merge.

acceptance.criterion: Database constraints prevent a party from having both or neither subtype and prevent invalid relationship references.
Valid emails and phone numbers normalize deterministically while invalid or incomplete values retain raw evidence and receive an explicit quality state.
acceptance.evidence: Normalization unit tests with workbook-derived examples

acceptance.criterion: Suppressed contact points cannot be selected for outreach and remain suppressed after edits, imports, and merges.
A stale edit receives a readable conflict response and cannot silently overwrite the newer record.
Archiving a party preserves its source evidence and historical relationships and removes it from default active lists.

features.title: Lead lifecycle, ownership, and stage history
features.user_story: As a sales representative, I need to own and advance leads through a clear pipeline without losing history or accountability.

requirements.statement: Model leads separately from parties and link people or organizations to leads using explicit roles.
Support campaign, current stage, data-readiness state, source attribution, created date, archive state, and a human-readable lead number.
Maintain append-only stage history with occurred time, actor, reason, and required stage-specific fields.
Maintain assignment history and enforce no more than one active primary owner while allowing configured team visibility.
Require open in-progress leads to have a valid next task or an explicit documented reason according to policy.
Use optimistic concurrency and atomic services for stage changes, reassignment, and related audit events.

acceptance.criterion: The lead current stage always equals the most recent accepted stage-history entry.
Invalid stage transitions or missing required reasons and fields are rejected without partial writes.
The database prevents two active primary owners for one lead and preserves previous assignments.
A seller cannot update, reassign, or transition an out-of-scope lead by changing a URL or request body.
Lead creation warns about existing party and lead candidates and creates the lead, party links, owner, source, and next task atomically.

features.title: Interactions, tasks, and lead timeline
features.user_story: As a seller, I need to log a contact and its next step quickly so the team always knows what happened and what comes next.

requirements.statement: Record interactions with one lead, occurrence date and optional exact time, direction, channel, outcome, participants, note, actor, and source.
Reject placeholders such as Sin accion as interactions and distinguish attempted contact, completed contact, and response using governed outcome semantics.
Support tasks with owner, due date, state, priority, completion/reschedule details, and optional link to the originating interaction.
Create interaction, optional stage update, next task, and audit event in one database transaction.
Present an ordered lead timeline that distinguishes occurrence time from entry time and includes stage and assignment history.
Retain date-only precision when the source does not justify an exact time.

acceptance.criterion: The quick-contact workflow validates lead, date, channel, and outcome and saves its interaction, next task, and audit event atomically.
Sin accion and equivalent non-events cannot create interaction rows or inflate contact metrics.
Task state and dates remain consistent: completion requires completion time, open tasks have no completion time, and overdue uses the team-local date.
The timeline is stable, correctly ordered, permission-scoped, and labels source versus user-entered events.
Representative sellers can complete the quick-contact workflow in under 60 seconds without technical assistance.

features.title: Today workspace and guided CRM navigation
features.user_story: As a non-technical seller, I need the application to tell me what needs attention without constructing a query or understanding the database.

requirements.statement: Provide top-level Today, My leads, Search, Reports, Data quality when authorized, and Help navigation.
Today shows overdue tasks, tasks due today, stale in-progress leads, new responses, and unassigned items visible to managers.
Order Today items by transparent urgency rules and let every item open the relevant lead or task.
The lead detail page combines identity, contacts, stage, owner, source summary, quality flags, timeline, and next task without exposing database terminology.
Provide useful empty states and one-click common actions with safe defaults for current user, current lead, date, and recent channel.

acceptance.criterion: A seller opening the application sees only their actionable, scope-authorized work without first configuring filters.
Overdue, due-today, stale, response, and unassigned classifications match fixed timezone-aware fixtures.
Every card and row has a clear next action, a readable empty state, and a direct path to its lead or task.
acceptance.evidence: Template tests and manual UX review

acceptance.criterion: The main navigation and lead page use plain Spanish labels and expose no table names, foreign keys, SQL vocabulary, or raw UUIDs.
acceptance.evidence: UI content review and rendered-page tests

features.title: Lossless spreadsheet import, staging, and lineage
features.user_story: As a data steward, I need to preview and reconcile an import before it changes canonical records while preserving every source row.

requirements.statement: Model source documents, import batches, source records, source coordinates, raw row payloads, checksums, parser version, status, and import actor.
Separate upload, staging, validation, candidate matching, approval, canonical application, and reconciliation into explicit states.
Preview row counts, errors, warnings, inferred changes, duplicates, unmatched activities, and canonical diffs before approval.
Make reruns idempotent by source checksum, source-row identity, deterministic normalization rules, and application version.
Require steward approval before canonical writes and apply each approved batch atomically or with a documented resumable transaction boundary.
Retain source-to-canonical links for parties, leads, contacts, interactions, tasks, aliases, and corrections.

acceptance.criterion: Uploading a workbook creates staging and preview records but causes no canonical business-data change before explicit approval.
Reprocessing the same checksum and parser version creates no duplicate canonical entities, contacts, leads, or interactions.
Every staged row retains workbook, sheet, row coordinate, raw values, classification, and resulting canonical links or rejection reason.
Malformed files, unexpected headers, formula errors, and oversized uploads fail safely with understandable Spanish diagnostics.
Only a data steward can approve or apply an import, and approval and application are audited separately.

out_of_scope: Unapproved automatic correction of ambiguous source data

features.title: Data-quality queue, matching, and governed merge
features.user_story: As a data steward, I need a prioritized evidence-based queue to correct invalid data and merge duplicates without losing provenance.

requirements.statement: Model quality issues with rule code, severity, affected source and canonical records, owner, state, decision, timestamps, and acceptance reason.
Generate deterministic exact candidates for normalized email, phone, and approved source identifiers and evidence-ranked fuzzy candidates for names and organizations.
Never auto-merge fuzzy candidates; present a side-by-side comparison, source evidence, confidence reasons, and affected links.
Merge through an atomic service that selects a survivor, preserves aliases and source links, redirects related records, respects suppression, and records chosen values.
Support split or reject decisions and retain rejected candidate decisions so the same pair is not repeatedly proposed without new evidence.
Show data-readiness and high-severity quality indicators to authorized users without overwhelming the normal seller workflow.

acceptance.criterion: Error, warning, and information issues sort predictably by severity and age and can be assigned, resolved, accepted with reason, or reopened.
Fuzzy similarity can only create a review candidate and never changes canonical relationships without steward approval.
A merge preview lists every lead, interaction, task, contact point, alias, and source link that will be affected.
After an approved merge, old identifiers resolve to the survivor, provenance remains traceable, and suppressed contact points remain suppressed.
Every merge, rejection, split, correction, and accepted warning records actor, reason, before state, after state, and source evidence.

out_of_scope: Destructive deletion of merged source evidence

features.title: Permission-scoped global search
features.user_story: As a seller, I need to find a prospect using a name, organization, email, phone, or note even when accents or a minor spelling error differ.

requirements.statement: Search parties, organizations, people, aliases, leads, normalized email and phone, and authorized notes through one understandable search box.
Combine exact identifier matching, normalized text, PostgreSQL full-text search, and pg_trgm similarity with deterministic ranking.
Apply row scope before ranking and pagination so result counts and snippets never leak unauthorized information.
Display why a result matched and enough identity context to distinguish similar parties without exposing sensitive details.
Use indexed queries, bounded input, stable pagination, and observable slow-query thresholds.

acceptance.criterion: Fixed fixtures are found by exact email, normalized phone, accented and unaccented names, organization alias, and one-character spelling variation.
Out-of-scope records affect neither returned rows, counts, ranking, suggestions, nor highlighted snippets.
Every result identifies its match reason and opens the correct permission-checked record.
Representative search requests meet the agreed 500 millisecond p95 server-response target at the initial-volume test dataset.
acceptance.evidence: Recorded performance test and query plans

acceptance.criterion: Empty, excessively long, wildcard-heavy, and malformed search input is handled safely without unbounded queries.

features.title: Guided filters, segments, and saved views
features.user_story: As a non-technical user, I need to build and save meaningful segments using business language instead of SQL.

requirements.statement: Provide allow-listed filters for lead stage, owner, campaign, readiness, source, age, staleness, geography, specialty, contactability, activity, response, and task state.
Support guided AND conditions and deliberately bounded OR groups without accepting column names, SQL fragments, or arbitrary expressions.
Always display a human-readable Spanish summary, result count, sort order, active filters, and easy reset controls.
Support private views and manager-approved shared views using versioned structured definitions rather than stored SQL.
Apply the same authorization scope to counts, results, saved-view execution, and subsequent exports.

acceptance.criterion: Each supported filter and operator maps to a validated typed value and a deterministic ORM query.
A saved view can be created, reopened, renamed, copied, archived, and executed without changing its meaning.
A user cannot execute another user private view or gain broader access through a manager shared view.
Pagination and sorting are stable and do not duplicate or omit records when several rows share the selected sort value.
Rendered filters use business labels and never expose database table names, raw field paths, or SQL syntax.

features.title: Metric catalog, dashboards, and governed reports
features.user_story: As a sales manager, I need reports with consistent definitions so I can trust pipeline, activity, response, source, follow-up, and data-quality decisions.

requirements.statement: Create governed definitions for contactable lead, contacted lead, response rate, stale lead, stage age, overdue task, and cohort conversion.
Every metric records owner, description, numerator, denominator, inclusion rules, timeframe semantics, version, and effective date.
Provide approved reports for attention today, pipeline distribution, contact activity, response, source performance, follow-up gaps, research needs, and time in stage.
Use read-only reporting services or database views that preserve authorization scope and isolate metric semantics from templates.
Show definition, selected timeframe, scope, filters, as-of timestamp, result count, and data-freshness indicator with each report.
Use stage history for stage age and conversion, interaction occurrence for contact metrics, and team-local dates for overdue work.

acceptance.criterion: Fixture datasets with known outcomes produce the approved value for every metric and report dimension.
Sin accion rows are excluded from contact and response measures, and response rate uses eligible outbound interactions rather than lead count.
Report rows, totals, and chart categories remain within the requesting user's authorized scope.
Every displayed KPI exposes its versioned definition, timeframe, scope, owner, and as-of time from the same page.
Standard dashboards meet the agreed 2 second p95 response target at the initial-volume test dataset.
acceptance.evidence: Performance test and database query plans

features.title: Governed exports
features.user_story: As an authorized user, I need to export a defined result set without bypassing scope, privacy, or audit controls.

requirements.statement: Require a separate export permission and reapply row and field scope at export execution time.
Support approved CSV and XLSX layouts with explicit column definitions, localized dates, stable codes when required, and no hidden sensitive fields.
Run large exports as bounded background jobs with status, expiry, retry policy, and access-controlled download.
Record requester, reason when required, report or saved-view definition, filters, scope, row count, fields, file checksum, and download events.
Protect spreadsheet exports against formula injection and use predictable UTF-8 and date representations.

acceptance.criterion: A user with view access but without export permission cannot create, inspect, or download an export through any endpoint.
Changing a saved view after requesting an export does not change the captured export definition, and scope is re-evaluated before file creation.
CSV and XLSX cells beginning with formula-control characters are neutralized without corrupting legitimate data.
Expired, deleted, or unauthorized export downloads are unavailable while their audit metadata remains retained according to policy.
Every successful and denied export attempt produces the appropriate audit event without logging file contents.

features.title: Audit, privacy, retention, and governed correction
features.user_story: As a privacy or audit reviewer, I need to trace sensitive actions and complete access, correction, suppression, and retention workflows consistently.

requirements.statement: Maintain append-only business audit events for authentication, authorization decisions, sensitive reads when required, creates, updates, stage changes, assignments, imports, merges, suppression, exports, and administration.
Audit events record actor, action, target, request correlation, reason, timestamp, and safe before/after changes without duplicating secrets or unrestricted note bodies.
Provide a permissioned workflow to locate all related personal data and record access, correction, update, suppression, and deletion-or-retention decisions.
Enforce contact suppression across manual outreach, reminders, imports, merges, reports, and exports.
Implement approved retention categories and legal-hold exceptions using reviewable jobs rather than silent destructive deletion.
Display policy guidance that prohibits patient or clinical data and provide an incident path for inappropriate sensitive content.

acceptance.criterion: Audit events are immutable to normal application and administrator roles and can be filtered only by authorized reviewers.
acceptance.evidence: Database permissions and application authorization tests

acceptance.criterion: A privacy reviewer can locate a person's parties, contact points, lead relationships, source lineage, interactions, exports, and suppression state from one governed workflow.
A suppressed contact point cannot reappear as contactable after a repeat import, party merge, reactivation, or saved-view execution.
Retention dry runs enumerate intended actions and require approved execution; legal-hold records are excluded and explained.
Application logs and audit events contain no passwords, tokens, database URLs, complete export contents, or unrestricted sensitive notes.
acceptance.evidence: Automated log-redaction tests and manual sample review

features.title: Transactional jobs, reminders, and notifications
features.user_story: As a seller, I need dependable reminders without receiving duplicate or excessive notifications.

requirements.statement: Implement a PostgreSQL transactional outbox with job type, payload reference, idempotency key, schedule, attempts, state, lease, and last safe error.
Run a separately deployable worker process using bounded polling, transaction-safe claiming, retry with backoff, and dead-letter review.
Create reminder jobs in the same transaction as task changes so committed work is eventually notified and rolled-back work is not.
Provide per-user notification preferences with digest by default and restricted escalation rules.
Expose failed jobs and retries to authorized operators without exposing secrets or full personal-data payloads.

acceptance.criterion: Repeated processing of the same idempotency key produces no duplicate reminder or export artifact.
A worker crash after claiming or sending a job recovers according to the documented lease and provider-idempotency behavior.
Completing, cancelling, or rescheduling a task cancels or replaces obsolete reminders.
Users receive the configured digest or escalation and can change permitted preferences from an accessible settings page.
Operator job screens are permission-scoped and redact sensitive payload fields and provider credentials.

out_of_scope: Redis, RabbitMQ, or Celery before measured need

features.title: Spanish-first accessible and responsive experience
features.user_story: As a non-technical user, I need every critical CRM workflow to be understandable, keyboard accessible, and usable on common desktop and phone screens.

requirements.statement: Target WCAG 2.2 AA for critical workflows with semantic HTML, visible focus, keyboard operation, sufficient contrast, status text, and accessible errors.
Use plain Spanish business labels, visible field labels, examples, contextual help, and a maintained glossary; do not rely on placeholders alone.
Use progressive disclosure so common fields appear first and technical lineage or research details remain available under clearly labeled detail sections.
Ensure normal links and forms remain functional without HTMX; enhanced fragments must preserve focus, history, validation, and error recovery.
Use responsive cards or controlled table overflow, 44-pixel-class touch targets, no drag-only interaction, and no meaning conveyed solely through color.
Provide contextual Help and a one-page Como trabajamos guide for Today, leads, contact logging, search, and data-quality workflows.

acceptance.criterion: Today to lead to log contact to create next task, search to saved view, and steward merge are usable using only the keyboard.
acceptance.evidence: Documented keyboard test and browser automation where practical

acceptance.criterion: Automated accessibility checks report no serious or critical violation on every critical page and state.
Critical pages remain understandable and operable at 200 percent zoom and at the agreed phone viewport without hidden required actions.
acceptance.evidence: Responsive manual test record and screenshots

acceptance.criterion: Disabling JavaScript still allows authentication fallback, navigation, search, data display, and ordinary create/edit form submission.
Form errors retain user input, identify the affected field in text, move focus appropriately, and explain how to correct the value in Spanish.
acceptance.evidence: Form-error integration and manual screen-reader tests

features.title: Application security and defense in depth
features.user_story: As the security owner, I need layered controls and executable evidence that sales and personal data cannot be accessed or changed outside policy.

requirements.statement: Require HTTPS, secure HttpOnly SameSite cookies, trusted proxy configuration, CSRF protection, clickjacking protection, HSTS after validation, and a restrictive content security policy.
Use parameterized ORM queries, output escaping, validated redirects, bounded uploads, safe filenames, request-size limits, and rate limits for authentication, search, export, and import.
Use least-privilege application, migration, reporting, backup, and operator roles and apply selective PostgreSQL row-level security where it provides defense in depth.
Store secrets in the deployment secret facility, rotate them under a documented process, and never include them in source, logs, jobs, exports, or error pages.
Run dependency vulnerability, static analysis, Django deployment, and security regression checks in CI and before release.
Maintain a threat model and verification checklist aligned with the selected OWASP ASVS 5.0 level.

acceptance.criterion: Automated tests reject CSRF bypass, horizontal and vertical authorization attempts, unsafe redirects, malicious uploads, and spreadsheet-formula payloads.
Production deployment checks pass and expected TLS, cookie, HSTS, framing, referrer, and content-security headers are present.
acceptance.evidence: Deployment check and HTTP header scan

acceptance.criterion: Direct SQL under each database role demonstrates only the privileges documented for that role, including tested RLS behavior where enabled.
Dependency and static scans contain no unresolved critical or high issue without a written, approved exception and expiry.
Production-style error responses disclose no stack trace, secret, database detail, or unauthorized record existence.

features.title: Deployment, observability, backups, and recovery
features.user_story: As the technical owner, I need repeatable deployment and observable recovery so the CRM remains reliable without depending on one person's memory.

requirements.statement: Build immutable container images for one web process type and one worker process type, using a production WSGI or ASGI server and non-root runtime user.
Maintain separate development, test, staging, and production configuration and databases with controlled promotion and migration steps.
Emit structured, correlated logs, metrics, and traces for web requests, database calls, jobs, imports, exports, authentication, and critical domain commands without sensitive payloads.
Define service-level indicators and alerts for availability, latency, error rate, database saturation, job backlog, import failures, and backup freshness.
Use managed PostgreSQL backups with point-in-time recovery, encrypted object storage for temporary artifacts, documented retention, and quarterly isolated restore drills.
Provide deployment, rollback, migration, incident, restore, credential-rotation, and worker-recovery runbooks.

acceptance.criterion: The same versioned image runs in staging and production with configuration supplied externally and no development server or embedded secret.
acceptance.evidence: Image inspection and staging deployment record

acceptance.criterion: A deployment can run preflight checks, apply migrations safely, verify readiness, and roll back application code according to the runbook.
An operator can trace a failed request or job using a correlation ID without viewing personal-data payloads.
A backup is restored into an isolated environment and passes login, row-count, lineage, and representative report checks within approved RPO and RTO.
Alerts fire and recover in controlled tests for web failure, database unavailability, stale backup, and excessive job backlog.

out_of_scope: A specific cloud-provider commitment before approval

features.title: Workbook migration rehearsal, reconciliation, and cutover
features.user_story: As the data owner, I need a repeatable migration that proves every workbook row and business record is accounted for before spreadsheet editing stops.

requirements.statement: Use the normalized workbook as the approved migration input while retaining the original workbook checksum and source coordinates as evidence.
Reconcile all 633 source rows, the 331 lead baseline, the 313 party baseline, the 151 atomic contact-point baseline, and every documented canonical transformation or exclusion.
Resolve all 28 error-level items and obtain an explicit decision for every remaining warning before production cutover.
Confirm the lead and occurrence date for all 34 interaction candidates, including the 22 exact links, 4 ambiguous candidates, and 8 unmatched candidates.
Perform empty-environment dry runs, owner worklist review, manager stage-count review, source-evidence review, and repeatable correction mapping before final import.
Execute a controlled spreadsheet freeze, checksum, final import, acceptance-query gate, go-live decision, and rollback plan that can reopen the prior process if acceptance fails.
Keep the source workbook read-only after cutover and operate a two-week hypercare queue before decommissioning spreadsheet editing.

acceptance.criterion: The reconciliation report accounts for every source row as imported, intentionally excluded, duplicate evidence, shell/header, or rejected with an approved reason.
There are zero unresolved error-level quality issues and every warning has a resolution or named owner-approved acceptance reason.
acceptance.evidence: Quality-issue export signed by the data owner

acceptance.criterion: All 34 interaction candidates have a confirmed lead/date decision and no accepted interaction is orphaned.
acceptance.evidence: Interaction reconciliation query and steward sign-off

acceptance.criterion: Running the final migration twice against equivalent empty databases yields identical canonical business keys, counts, issue states, and report results.
Sales owners validate assigned worklists, managers validate stage totals, and the data owner approves lineage and migration exceptions before cutover.
A rehearsed rollback can discard the new production database safely and restore the previous sales process within the approved cutover window.

features.title: System validation, UAT, training, and launch readiness
features.user_story: As the product owner, I need independent evidence, trained users, and approved launch gates before the CRM becomes the system of record.

requirements.statement: Run unit, PostgreSQL constraint, integration, permission matrix, browser journey, migration, reporting, accessibility, security, performance, and recovery verification.
Execute role-based UAT for Today, lead creation, contact logging, stage change, tasks, search, saved views, merge, import, reports, export, and privacy workflows.
Train sales champions, sellers, managers, data stewards, privacy reviewers, and operators using role-specific Spanish material and a staging environment.
Instrument adoption, activity freshness, task hygiene, contactability, quality, report trust, usability, reliability, and support demand without invasive employee surveillance.
Require product, data, security/privacy, reporting, operations, and user-adoption sign-offs and record all accepted residual risks.
Treat failed security tests, unresolved migration errors, incorrect permission scope, unreconciled reports, failed restore, inaccessible critical workflows, or missing runbooks as release blockers.

acceptance.criterion: The full release verification suite passes against the release candidate and production-equivalent PostgreSQL configuration.
Every critical UAT journey is completed by its intended role with no unresolved release-blocking finding.
The quick-contact median is below 60 seconds and representative users can start the day, find a lead, and understand the next action without technical assistance.
All required product, data, metric, privacy/security, operations, migration, training, and go-live approvals are recorded with approver and date.
Hypercare ownership, severity definitions, support channel, escalation path, daily review schedule, and rollback authority are documented and staffed.
No release blocker remains open and each accepted non-blocking risk has an owner, mitigation, expiry, and review date.

out_of_scope: Features not represented by approved backlog changes
